description: Publish the first packaged install path for the product: a publishable manifest under the new name, four cross-compiled binaries released as prerelease assets, a curl-able installer, honest install docs, and the executable instruction files migrated to the new typed command.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms single-host cross-compilation for standalone executables: bun build --compile --target=bun-<os>-<arch> <entrypoint> --outfile <out>, with bun-darwin-arm64, bun-darwin-x64, bun-linux-x64 and bun-linux-arm64 all listed as supported CompileTarget values. No deprecation affecting the four targets this PRD needs; --outfile is required because --outdir is unsupported under --compile. macOS codesign of the produced binary is documented as the Gatekeeper remedy, matching the ad-hoc re-sign already in scripts/build-release.sh.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: `gship claude --help` still prints the retired command 7 times (title…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [src/commands/claude.ts:28]: `gship claude --help` still prints the retired command 7 times (title :26 'cam claude', usage :28 'cam claude [args...]', Examples :39-41, Config :63). This violates US-002 AC1's own prose, which requires that 'nem o help de topo nem o help de QUALQUER subcomando imprime o comando velho'. The AC is green only because its oracle enumerates 12 subcommands (init config run plan journal patterns suggestions next review ship tag status) and omits `claude`; src/commands/claude.ts was never touched by this branch (git diff main...HEAD --stat for it is empty). Since install.sh installs only gateship and gship, a freshly-installed user reading `gship claude --help` is told to type `cam claude -p "Hello world"`, a command that does not exist on their machine. This is the identical blind-oracle defect class as US-R1-002, on a surface its scope did not reach. Fix: rename the title/usage/Examples strings in src/commands/claude.ts, and widen AC1's oracle to enumerate every registered subcommand (or derive the list) so the guard cannot go tautological again.

userStories.description: CRITICAL [src/commands/plan.ts:119]: 15 user-facing RUNTIME remediation strings still instruct the retired command, so the binary tells a stuck user to type something their machine does not have: plan.ts:119,132; ship.ts:175,191; next.ts:316,332,387; review.ts:172,188; issue.ts:147; spec.ts:181; run.ts:1005; setup.ts:654,770; pause.ts:82; src/logging/screen.ts:113 (e.g. 'Run `cam run` manually, then retry `cam ship`.'). userStories.title: WARNING: `${{ github.ref_name }}` is interpolated directly into a `run:` shell…
userStories.description: WARNING [.github/workflows/release.yml:34]: `${{ github.ref_name }}` is interpolated directly into a `run:` shell block at lines 34 and 40. GitHub's security-hardening guide states that 'for inline scripts, the preferred approach to handling untrusted input is to set the value of the expression to an intermediate environment variable' (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions). git check-ref-format permits characters this pattern is sensitive to (`;`, `"`, `$`, backtick, parentheses) since it forbids only space, `~`, `^`, `:`, `?`, `*`, `[` and `\`, so a crafted tag name can break out of the double-quoted argument. Exploitation requires push access, which bounds the severity, but this is a brand-new file and the fix is mechanical: add `env: TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}` and reference `"$TAG"` in the script.

userStories.title: WARNING: install.sh's success path has zero execution coverage. The suite cover…
userStories.description: WARNING [test/install-sh.test.ts:64]: install.sh's success path has zero execution coverage. The suite covers two error paths (empty release list, curl failure) plus `bash -n`, but never the happy path, so the behaviour the story actually promises (download the asset, install BOTH `gateship` and `gship`, chmod +x, strip the macOS quarantine bit, and remain additive over a pre-existing `cam`) is asserted only by static grep in US-004's oracles. That is the same class of gap that let US-R1-001 ship: the oracles were `test -f` / `grep` / `bash -n`, and nothing executed the script. The existing fake-curl PATH shim already makes this cheap: have the shim write a dummy payload for the `-o` download call, then assert both destination files exist and are executable, and that a pre-created `cam` file in the install dir survives untouched. Per the test-quality triad this is the missing success leg.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: The installer's tag-resolution error path is unreachable dead code an…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [install.sh:65]: The installer's tag-resolution error path is unreachable dead code and the installer dies silently. Under `set -euo pipefail` (install.sh:31), the assignment TAG="$(curl -fsSL .../releases | grep -m1 '\"tag_name\"' | sed ...)" aborts the whole script the moment grep finds nothing (exit 1), so the friendly guard at install.sh:66-69 ('ERROR: could not resolve the latest release tag from the GitHub API') can never run. Verified live by the reviewer: GATESHIP_INSTALL_DIR=$(mktemp -d) bash install.sh prints only '[install] resolving the latest release tag...' and exits 1 with no message on stdout or stderr, leaving the install dir empty. This is the state every user hits today (no Release exists yet), and it is also the behaviour on a GitHub API rate-limit 403 or any network failure, since curl -f exits non-zero inside the same substitution. US-004's oracles only run `test -f`, `grep` and `bash -n` against install.sh, so nothing executes it. Fix: capture the curl output and the tag in separate steps whose failure is checked explicitly (e.g. `if ! body=$(curl -fsSL ...); then <message>; fi`, then parse), so every failure mode prints a diagnostic before exiting non-zero.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: US-005's acceptance criteria 1 and 2 are green only because their ext…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [.claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md:264]: US-005's acceptance criteria 1 and 2 are green only because their extractor is blind, not because the migration is complete. Both oracles terminate the command token on `( |$)`, which cannot match the backtick-delimited form ``cam run`` that is the dominant form in these markdown files. Re-running the same extractor with the terminator widened to ([^a-zA-Z0-9_-]|$) finds 66 remaining `cam <cmd>` typed-command instructions inside the exact AC1 scope (.claude/agents 15, .claude/commands 15, .claude/skills 1, scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md 4, templates/ mirror 31) and 46 inside the AC2 scope (src/vendor/_generated.ts: `cam next` x14, `cam run` x7, `cam init` x4, `cam plan` x4, `cam prune` x4, `cam review` x4, `cam ship` x4, `cam issue` x3, `cam decide` x1, `cam stop` x1). These are imperative instructions, not historical prose: subagent-orchestrator.md:264 reads '`gship decide <option>`. Removed only once the operator's `cam decide` call' (one sentence, half renamed); :558 says 'restart `cam run` before retrying'; .claude/commands/cam-spec.md:20 says 'ask the operator to pause it (`cam stop` ...)'. Because install.sh installs only gateship/gship, a fresh user's `gship init` writes these templates and the embedded blob then tells the agent to type a command that machine does not have, which is precisely the failure US-005 exists to prevent. Fix: widen the migration (and both oracles) to the ([^a-zA-Z0-9_-]|$) terminator, re-run embed-vendor, keeping the four history files pinned as before.

userStories.title: Tornar o manifesto publicavel sob o nome do produto e sincronizar o lockfile
userStories.description: As a stranger evaluating the project, I need the package manifest to declare a real, publishable package with an executable name, so that the packaging path has a coherent starting point instead of a private manifest with no binary.
acceptanceCriteria: O manifesto e publicavel sob o nome do produto: private deixa de ser true, name passa a gateship, e bin, files, license, repository e engines passam a existir. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'test "$(jq -r .private package.json)" != "true" && test "$(jq -r .bin package.json)" != "null" && test "$(jq -r .license package.json)" != "null" && test "$(jq -r .files package.json)" != "null" && test "$(jq -r .repository package.json)" != "null" && test "$(jq -r .engines package.json)" != "null" && test "$(jq -r .name package.json)" = "gateship"'] (ESPECIE: change-detection. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-01: name=cam-runtime, private=true, e os cinco campos ausentes.)

O mapa bin expoe os dois nomes canonicos decididos pelo ADR-0054. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'test "$(jq -r .bin.gateship package.json)" != "null" && test "$(jq -r .bin.gship package.json)" != "null"'] (ESPECIE: change-detection. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-01: bin ausente, os dois lados null.)

O lockfile acompanha o rename do manifesto no mesmo commit, senao o required check do CI reprova com todos os gates locais verdes. [oracle: named-command bash -c '! grep -qF "cam-runtime" bun.lock && grep -qF "gateship" bun.lock && bun install --frozen-lockfile'] (ESPECIE: change-detection, forma livre de literal numerico. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-03 pela orquestradora, exit 1: bun.lock:6 carrega o nome antigo no workspace raiz, 1 ocorrencia, e 0 de gateship. O .github/workflows/ci.yml roda bun install --frozen-lockfile nas linhas 24 e 78 como parte do check obrigatorio, e nenhum gate local roda frozen-lockfile, entao a divergencia entre package.json e bun.lock e invisivel a typecheck, bun test e check:all e so aparece no PR, travando a fase de ship. ATENCAO AO DESENHO DO ORACULO: o oraculo sugerido pelo auditor usava jq sobre bun.lock e foi medido INVALIDO, porque bun.lock nao e JSON parseavel por jq, erro de parse na linha 17; o criterio falharia por erro de comando e nao por assercao. Por isso este usa grep de string fixa mais o proprio frozen-lockfile. Origem: F-03 important do audit round 2 deste issue.)

PIN DE INVARIANCIA: a fonte da versao continua sendo src/version.ts e o manifesto publicavel nao diverge dela, comparando derivado ao vivo dos dois lados e nao congelado. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'test "$(jq -r .version package.json)" = "$(grep -oE "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" src/version.ts | head -1)"'] (ESPECIE: pin de invariancia, verde por construcao. CRITERIO AUTORAL, varrido pela planner na main 2026-08-03, exit 0 VERDE: os dois lados leem a mesma versao. Varrido VERMELHO contra divergencia simulada. Existe porque tornar o manifesto publicavel cria uma segunda aparencia de fonte-de-versao, e o gotcha do issue exige que as duas nunca divirjam.)
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
A espinha de qualidade passa. [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Arquivos: package.json, bun.lock. LICENSE ja existe na raiz, entao o campo license descreve o que ja esta la. O nome canonico e gateship e o alias digitado e gship (ADR-0054, decisao parte 1); o mapa bin expoe os dois. NPM NAO E PUBLICADO NESTE CICLO (ADR-0055): o objetivo e tornar publicavel, nao publicar, entao nao rode nenhum npm publish nem bun publish. index.ts nao tem shebang hoje (linha 1 e comentario), entao se bin apontar para ./index.ts adicione o shebang no mesmo commit ou aponte bin para o entrypoint que o build produz; escolha uma das duas e seja consistente com o campo files. engines deve refletir o runtime real: CLAUDE.md exige Bun >= 1.2 e o toolchain pinado em .bun-version e 1.3.14. A versao continua vindo de src/version.ts (parseada em scripts/build-release.sh:49-54); package.json apenas espelha, nunca vira a fonte. Ordem de trabalho do lockfile: edite package.json, rode bun install (sem --frozen) para regravar o nome do workspace raiz em bun.lock:6, e so entao valide com bun install --frozen-lockfile; .github/workflows/ci.yml roda --frozen-lockfile nas linhas 24 e 78 e nenhum gate local roda, entao a divergencia so apareceria no PR e travaria a fase de ship.

userStories.title: Renomear a superficie digitada do binario (help, usage, --version) e desancorar o gate agents-md do prefixo aposentado
userStories.description: As a newly installed user, I need the binary help and version output to name the command I actually have, so that nothing the product prints teaches me to type a command that no longer exists.
acceptanceCriteria: O help do binario nao instrui um recem-instalado a digitar o comando aposentado: nem o help de topo nem o help de qualquer subcomando imprime o comando velho, e o nome novo aparece no help de topo. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'bun index.ts --help | grep -q gship || exit 1; for c in init config run plan journal patterns suggestions next review ship tag status; do bun index.ts $c --help | grep -qE "(^|[^a-zA-Z_/-])cam " && exit 1; done; ! bun index.ts --help | grep -qE "(^|[^a-zA-Z_/-])cam "'] (ESPECIE: change-detection, forma livre de literal numerico. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-03 pela orquestradora, exit 1: 1 match no help de topo, 22 matches somados nos helps dos doze subcomandos, e 0 ocorrencias de gship. Cumpre a ADR-0054 linha 96, que manda documentation, help output e usage strings migrarem, e que a AC7 nao cobre porque varre arquivos de instrucao e nao o binario. ATENCAO AO DESENHO DO ORACULO: o oraculo sugerido pelo auditor varria SO bun index.ts --help contra a lista de subcomandos e foi medido VERDE na main, ou seja nasceria tautologico, porque o help de topo lista os subcomandos SEM o prefixo e as usage strings vivem nos campos usage: de index.ts, alcancaveis so pelo help de cada subcomando. Este oraculo varre os dois niveis de proposito. Origem: F-02 critical do audit round 2 deste issue.)

O binario tambem se identifica pelo nome novo no --version, nao apenas no help. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'bun index.ts --version | grep -qE "^gateship [0-9]"'] (ESPECIE: change-detection, forma livre de literal numerico. CRITERIO AUTORAL, varrido pela planner na main 2026-08-03, exit 1 VERMELHO: index.ts:2919 imprime o nome aposentado seguido da versao. Existe porque a AC do help varre apenas --help e o smoke de scripts/build-release.sh compara a saida de --version contra uma string com o nome antigo, entao sem este criterio o nome aposentado sobrevive na unica saida que o instalador novo manda o usuario conferir.)

O gate agents-md continua checando os claims depois do rename: o extrator deixa de fixar o prefixo do comando aposentado, e existe teste durable provando que um comando desconhecido num arquivo varrido ainda produz finding. [oracle: named-command bash -c '! grep -qF "CAM_CMD_RE = /^cam" scripts/validate-agents-md.ts && bun test test/validate-agents-md.test.ts -t "comando desconhecido em arquivo varrido gera finding"'] (ESPECIE: change-detection, forma livre de literal numerico. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-03 pela orquestradora, exit 1: scripts/validate-agents-md.ts:221 fixa o extrator em CAM_CMD_RE ancorado no comando velho, e o teste nomeado nao existe. A falsificabilidade do -t foi confirmada a parte: bun test -t com nome inexistente sai 1, entao o criterio nao pode ficar verde por ausencia de teste. Sem este criterio o rename exigido pela AC7 faz 37 dos 52 claims da superficie varrida pararem de ser checados enquanto check:all segue verde, ou seja converte uma guarda shipada em tautologia sem que nenhum oraculo da propria story consiga perceber. O arquivo de teste test/validate-agents-md.test.ts ja existe e e onde o teste novo entra. Origem: F-01 critical do audit round 2 deste issue.)

PIN DE INVARIANCIA: os cinco contratos internos do ADR-0054 NAO renomeiam neste ciclo. As contagens de CAM_, .cam-, do socket tmux -L cam e de /cam- em src mais index.ts ficam identicas as da main, comparando derivado ao vivo e nao congelado. A vivacidade do extrator e provada pelo codigo de saida de git grep -q, nao por comparacao contra inteiro. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'for pat in "CAM_" "\.cam-" "tmux -L cam|\-L., ?.cam" "/cam-"; do git grep -qE "$pat" main -- src index.ts || exit 1; b=$(git grep -cE "$pat" main -- src index.ts | awk -F: "{s+=\$NF} END{print s}"); a=$(grep -rcE "$pat" src index.ts | awk -F: "{s+=\$NF} END{print s}"); test "$b" = "$a" || exit 1; done'] (ESPECIE: pin de invariancia, verde por construcao. Varrido VERDE na main 2026-08-01 com CAM_=164, .cam-=153, socket=15, /cam-=205; varrido VERMELHO contra drift simulada. Este pin substitui o AC5 do spec anterior, que pinava TODO rename e por isso contradizia o ADR-0054; aqui o pin proibe so as cinco camadas internas, e permite explicitamente o rename do binario e do comando digitado.)
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
A espinha de qualidade passa. [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Arquivos: index.ts, scripts/validate-agents-md.ts, test/validate-agents-md.test.ts, scripts/build-release.sh (duas linhas). O help e centralizado: renderHelp monta um bloco por comando (index.ts:116 topo, depois ~25 blocos ate index.ts:1090) e o guard central --help/-h dispara antes do switch via HELP_REGISTRY (patterns.md:678, CAM-211). O help de topo lista subcomandos SEM prefixo, entao o prefixo aposentado vive nos campos usage: de cada bloco, alcancaveis so pelo help de cada subcomando: e por isso que o oraculo herdado varre os dois niveis. Prosa usa o nome do produto (Gateship), exemplos digitados usam o alias (gship), conforme ADR-0054. O --version imprime em index.ts:2919; ao muda-lo, mova NO MESMO STORY as duas strings esperadas do smoke em scripts/build-release.sh (EXPECTED por volta de :83 e EXPECTED_INST por volta de :139), senao o script quebra por nome e nao por comportamento, e a US-003 herda a falha. O extrator do gate esta em scripts/validate-agents-md.ts:221 (CAM_CMD_RE ancorado no comando velho): desancore para que um comando desconhecido continue virando finding depois do rename, e escreva o teste durable com o nome EXATO 'comando desconhecido em arquivo varrido gera finding' em test/validate-agents-md.test.ts (o -t do bun test sai 1 quando nenhum teste casa, entao o nome tem que bater literalmente). Varra o teste novo VERMELHO contra o extrator atual antes de considera-lo falsificavel. O PIN dos cinco contratos internos esta aqui de proposito: editar help em index.ts e a forma mais provavel de mexer sem querer em /cam-, CAM_ ou .cam-, que este ciclo NAO renomeia (ADR-0054, sequenciamento; o rename interno e o ciclo seguinte). Oraculo de comportamento de CLI invoca bun index.ts <sub>, nunca o binario instalado (regra 5 do bloco curado).

userStories.notes: Arquivos: scripts/build-release.sh, .github/workflows/<novo>.yml. UM RUNNER SO: bun cross-compila, medido pela planner em 2026-08-03 num Mac arm64 com file confirmando cada saida (darwin-arm64 Mach-O arm64 61 MB, darwin-x64 Mach-O x86_64 66 MB, linux-x64 ELF x86-64 98 MB, linux-arm64 ELF aarch64 98 MB); os quatro juntos levaram menos de um segundo de compile. NAO use matriz de runners e NAO use macos-13: o round 1 deste issue morreu porque essa imagem foi aposentada em 2025-12-08 e o leg darwin-x64 nunca produzia asset enquanto o grep no workflow seguia verde. Docs oficiais confirmam a forma bun build --compile --target=bun-<os>-<arch> <entrypoint> --outfile <saida> e listam os quatro triples (fetch registrado em officialDocsConsulted); o --target de bun build --help NAO documenta esses triples, entao nao conclua ausencia a partir do help. Escolha o runner macOS para o job de Release: codesign so existe la e os dois artefatos darwin precisam da re-assinatura ad-hoc que scripts/build-release.sh:69 e :139 ja fazem; nao tente assinar os ELF. O smoke de --version so pode rodar no artefato nativo do host; para os outros tres verifique a arquitetura com file, nao execute. O teto de 100 MB do script tem folga apertada nos dois alvos linux (98 MB medidos): se ele passar a abortar, trate como sinal real, nao afrouxe sem justificativa. Convencao de nome de artefato, que a US-004 consome: gateship-darwin-arm64, gateship-darwin-x64, gateship-linux-x64, gateship-linux-arm64. O Release e prerelease por decisao registrada no ADR-0055 (mantem aberta a janela de rename do ADR-0054). scripts/check-ci-parity.ts le SOMENTE .github/workflows/ci.yml (CI_YML_PATH), entao um workflow novo de release nao entra na parity e nao deve ser adicionado ao ci.yml. INSTALACAO ADITIVA E RESTRICAO: o --install passa a criar gateship e gship no destino e NUNCA remove o cam ja instalado (o loop se auto-spawna pelo binario em cinco lugares, run.ts:740/822/853/895 e sidecar-liveness-watch.ts:92); o default de DEST em :130 aponta hoje para o nome aposentado. Pattern relevante: patterns.md:322 (soft-check de build-release deve sondar a presenca do prerequisito antes de tolerar exit nao-zero) e patterns.md:244 (toda resposta obrigatoria nova do init exige atualizar o smoke).

acceptanceCriteria: Existe um instalador curl-avel que baixa do Release, instala os dois nomes, e NAO remove o cam existente. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-01: nenhum install.sh existe no repo.)

O instalador e shell valido e mapeia os quatro alvos, nao apenas a maquina do autor. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'test -f install.sh && bash -n install.sh && for a in darwin-arm64 darwin-x64 linux-x64 linux-arm64; do grep -qF "$a" install.sh || exit 1; done'] (ESPECIE: change-detection, forma livre de literal numerico. CRITERIO AUTORAL, varrido pela planner na main 2026-08-03, exit 1 VERMELHO: nenhum install.sh existe. Existe porque o criterio herdado do instalador nao exige que ele seja parseavel nem que cubra os quatro alvos, e um instalador que so conhece um alvo devolve 404 em todo Mac Intel e em todo Linux, que e a mesma classe de falha do round 1.)

O README documenta a instalacao empacotada e diz a verdade sobre o que a assinatura garante: ad-hoc, NAO notarizada, com o comando de remediacao que o usuario realmente digita. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'grep -q "releases/download" README.md && grep -q "xattr -d com.apple.quarantine" README.md && grep -qi "not notarized" README.md'] (ESPECIE: fidelidade de evidencia, regra 4 do bloco curado. Varrido VERMELHO na main 2026-08-01: zero ocorrencias de releases/download. E varrido VERMELHO tambem contra uma copia FABRICADA plausivel em /tmp que contem releases/download e afirma 'fully notarized by Apple and run without any additional steps': a copia fabricada da exit 1 e a honesta da exit 0, entao o oraculo distingue prosa inventada de prosa fiel, nao apenas presenca de token.)

userStories.notes: Arquivos: install.sh (novo, na raiz), README.md. O instalador detecta os/arch e baixa de https://github.com/eduardocaminha/cam-cli/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>, com os nomes de asset fixados pela US-003: gateship-darwin-arm64, gateship-darwin-x64, gateship-linux-x64, gateship-linux-arm64. Instala em diretorio user-owned (default ~/.local/bin, sem sudo) e cria os DOIS nomes, gateship e gship. NUNCA remove nem sobrescreve um cam existente: a remocao e passo deliberado do operador depois do ciclo (ADR-0055, ultima consequencia). Um binario BAIXADO recebe a quarentena do Gatekeeper, diferente de um compilado local, entao o texto tem que trazer o comando que o usuario realmente digita: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <caminho>. Sem conta Apple Developer (decisao do operador 2026-08-01) os binarios saem ad-hoc assinados e NAO notarizados; o README ja carrega a ressalva honesta nas linhas 62-67 (Public distribution note), que deve ser ESTENDIDA e nunca contradita. O oraculo herdado do README foi desenhado para distinguir prosa fiel de prosa inventada: uma copia fabricada afirmando notarizacao completa da exit 1. Nao escreva que da para instalar via npm: o manifesto fica publicavel mas NAO e publicado neste ciclo (ADR-0055). A secao Install atual do README documenta so o caminho from-source e deve passar a liderar com o caminho empacotado, mantendo o from-source como alternativa. README.md nao esta em scripts/file-size-budget.json, entao nao ha teto a levantar.

findings.text: Layer B oracle FAIL: US-005's history-invariance PIN is RED at HEAD. The oracle compares per-file counts of `cam <subcommand>` between main and the branch across the four history files; scripts/cam/patterns.md drifted 41 -> 42, so the directive exits 1. Reviewer located the origin by walking git rev-list: the count flipped at commit aba8cb10 (US-R2-002) and stayed 42 through the 8 following commits, yet scripts/cam/prd.json still records US-005 with "passes": true. The cause is the appended US-R2-002 lesson at patterns.md:1196, which quotes the origin-label examples "`cam spec --write-docs: <detail>`" / "`cam spec --persist: <detail>`"; those two "`cam spec " tokens match the pin's regex. Nuance for fix-scoping: `git diff main...HEAD -- scripts/cam/patterns.md` has ZERO deleted lines, so no historical prose was rewritten and the pin's intent holds; only its exact-count mechanism is red. Fix is mechanical: reword the two quoted tokens in the new bullet (e.g. close the backtick immediately, `cam spec`, so the trailing-space boundary no longer matches), then re-run the directive. Full evidence in scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt.

US-R2-002 fixed only the runtime remediation strings its description enumerated by hand, leaving ~10 structurally identical siblings that still instruct the retired command at the moment of failure: drain.ts:108,119,122 ("Run `cam drain --clear`" / "Run `cam drain --stop`"), next.ts:193 ("run `cam stop` to clear"), src/retry/launcher.ts:309 ("Use `cam run` to open the orchestrator session"), stats.ts:247 ("or `cam init` first"), setup-merge-mode.ts:89 ("re-run `cam init`"), dashboard.ts:292 ("`cam stop` to clear"), resume.ts:475 and resume.ts:645 ("Re-run `cam next`"). Because install.sh installs only `gateship` and `gship`, a freshly-installed user hitting any of these paths is told to type a command that does not exist on their machine, which is exactly the defect class this story exists to close. scripts/cam/patterns.md defends the omission as "scope creep past what was asked... left as an open finding for a future story"; per the merit-over-cost rule a deferral-to-a-future-story rationale does not convert the weakness into an accepted trade-off. Note this is the third occurrence of the same hand-typed-enumeration blind spot on this branch (US-002 -> US-R2-001, US-005 -> US-R1-002, US-R2-002 -> this), and unlike the first two, US-R2-002 carries no oracle at all, so nothing mechanically guards the sweep. Deriving the sweep set from a single source of truth (as test/help-registry.test.ts now does for help text) would close the class rather than the instances.

Tag resolution parses the GitHub API JSON with `grep -m1 '"tag_name"' | sed`, which depends on the list-releases endpoint's created_at-descending ordering and on the first tag_name in the payload being the newest release. This is documented in the header comment and works today, but it is brittle against any response-shape change. If jq is acceptable as an installer dependency (it is already used by the US-001 oracles), `jq -r '.[0].tag_name'` would be exact; otherwise the current form is a reasonable trade-off for a dependency-free installer.

The new success-path test is solid (asserts the exec bit via statSync mode & 0o111 and byte-identity of a pre-existing `cam`, not mere existence). Two branches remain unexercised: the unsupported-OS/arch guards (install.sh:38,46,54) and the GATESHIP_VERSION pin path (install.sh:61-62) that skips API resolution entirely. Both are cheap to add with the existing PATH-shim harness and would complete the boundary leg of the triad.

The new release workflow has no static validation in the quality spine. scripts/check-ci-parity.ts reads only .github/workflows/ci.yml by construction, so release.yml is invisible to every local gate; a YAML or expression error surfaces only on a real tag push, which is the one moment it must not fail. Consider an actionlint step or extending the parity checker to lint sibling workflow files.
